```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("_common.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(ape); library(treeio); library(ggtree); library(ggtreeExtra)
  library(ggnewscale); library(ggbeeswarm)
})
kd <- function(f) repo_path("KyphosusMAGs", "data", f)
```

::: {.paper-links}
[Paper: Oliver *et al.* 2024, *mBio*](https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.00496-24)
[Code: KyphosusMAGs](https://github.com/AaronAOliver/KyphosusMAGs)
[Data: MAGs on Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8277654)
[SRA PRJNA819194 / PRJNA1023379](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/bioproject/PRJNA1023379)
:::

Herbivorous *Kyphosus* fish (nenue, or rudderfish) live on red, green and brown
seaweed and rely on gut microbes to break down its polysaccharides. Algal
glycans such as agar, carrageenan, alginate, fucoidan and ulvan are heavily
sulfated, so the industrial enzymes used for land plants work poorly on them.
We recovered metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from wild fish guts and from
bioreactors seeded with gut contents, and identified which microbes carry the
enzymes for each step of degradation.

This notebook rebuilds the main analyses from the processed tables in the
repository. Most figures are interactive: hover for values, click legend entries
to hide groups, and drag to zoom.

```{r load-data}
bin_taxa    <- read.delim(kd("bin_taxa.tab"))
bin_cazy    <- read.delim(kd("bin_cazy.tab"), check.names = FALSE)
bin_source  <- read.delim(kd("bin_source.tab"))
bin_scfa    <- read.delim(kd("bin_scfa.tab"))
bin_sulf    <- read.delim(kd("bin_sulf_reduct.tab"), check.names = FALSE)
bin_bgc     <- read.delim(kd("bin_bgc.tab"), check.names = FALSE)
bin_quality <- read.delim(kd("bin_quality.txt"))

mags <- bin_taxa %>%
  rename(MAG = bin, Taxonomy = taxa, `Genome size (bp)` = size,
         CGCs = cgcs, `CGC genes` = cgcgenes) %>%
  left_join(bin_cazy %>% rename(MAG = bins), by = "MAG") %>%
  left_join(bin_source %>% select(MAG = bins, Source), by = "MAG") %>%
  left_join(bin_scfa %>% select(MAG = MAG_id, Acetate, Propanoate, Butyrate), by = "MAG") %>%
  left_join(bin_sulf %>% rename(MAG = MAG_id), by = "MAG") %>%
  left_join(bin_bgc %>% count(MAG, name = "BGCs"), by = "MAG") %>%
  mutate(BGCs = replace_na(BGCs, 0))

study_mags <- filter(mags, Source != "Database Relative")
nice <- function(x) str_replace(x, " Algae CaZy", " algal CAZymes")   # "Red Algae CaZy" -> "Red algal CAZymes"

tibble(
  Quantity = c("MAGs with CAZyme annotations (fish gut + bioreactor)", "High-quality MAGs",
               "Biosynthetic gene clusters", "BGCs far from any known gene cluster family"),
  Count = c(nrow(study_mags), sum(bin_quality$High.Quality), nrow(bin_bgc), sum(bin_bgc$novel))
) %>% knitr::kable()
```

## Workflow

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 7
flowchart LR
  A[Wild Kyphosus gut<br/>metagenomes] --> C
  B[Bioreactor enrichments<br/>fed macroalgae] --> C
  C[Assembly + binning<br/>MAG QC] --> D[PhyloPhlAn<br/>phylogenomics]
  C --> E[dbCAN + SulfAtlas<br/>CAZymes & sulfatases]
  C --> F[gutSMASH<br/>SCFA pathways]
  C --> G[antiSMASH + BiG-SLiCE<br/>BGC novelty]

```

## Read-based taxonomy

Unassembled reads were classified with Kraken2 before binning. Compared with the wild fish guts, the
bioreactors are enriched in Bacillota (23% vs. 6% of reads on average) and
Desulfovibrionales (11% vs. 2%), and fewer of their reads are left
unclassified.

```{r read-taxonomy}
#| fig-height: 5
taxa_cols <- c("Bacillota", "Bacteroidota", "Gammaproteobacteria", "Alphaproteobacteria",
               "Desulfovibrionales", "Verrucomicrobiota", "Spirochaetota", "Fusobacteriota",
               "Fibrobacterota", "WOR.3", "Eukaryota", "Other.Taxa")
reads <- read.delim(kd("read_taxonomy.tab")) %>%
  filter(source %in% c("grey", "lightblue")) %>%
  mutate(Group = if_else(source == "grey", "Bioreactor enrichment", "Wild fish gut")) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(taxa_cols), names_to = "Taxon", values_to = "Fraction") %>%
  mutate(Taxon = recode(Taxon, WOR.3 = "WOR-3", Other.Taxa = "Other Taxa"),
         Taxon = factor(Taxon, levels = rev(recode(taxa_cols, WOR.3 = "WOR-3", Other.Taxa = "Other Taxa"))))

make_bar <- function(d, show) {
  plot_ly(d, x = ~id, y = ~Fraction, color = ~Taxon, colors = tax_colors,
          type = "bar", legendgroup = ~Taxon, showlegend = show,
          hovertemplate = "%{x}<br>%{fullData.name}: %{y:.1%}<extra></extra>") %>%
    layout(barmode = "stack", yaxis = list(tickformat = ".0%"))
}
subplot(
  make_bar(filter(reads, Group == "Bioreactor enrichment"), TRUE),
  make_bar(filter(reads, Group == "Wild fish gut"), FALSE),
  shareY = TRUE, widths = c(.4, .6), margin = .02
) %>% dark_layout(
  yaxis = list(title = "Fraction of classified reads", tickformat = ".0%"),
  xaxis = list(tickangle = -45), xaxis2 = list(tickangle = -45),
  legend = list(traceorder = "reversed", title = list(text = "<b>Taxon</b>")),
  annotations = list(
    list(text = "<b>Bioreactor enrichments</b>", x = .2, y = 1.06, xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
         xanchor = "center", showarrow = FALSE),
    list(text = "<b>Wild fish guts</b>", x = .71, y = 1.06, xref = "paper", yref = "paper",
         xanchor = "center", showarrow = FALSE)),
  margin = list(t = 40))
```

Binning recovered between 1 and 25 MAGs per sample. Samples starting with R
are bioreactors, and the others are wild fish guts.

```{r mag-quality}
#| fig-height: 3.5
bin_quality %>%
  pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "Quality", values_to = "MAGs") %>%
  mutate(Quality = factor(str_replace(Quality, "\\.Quality", " quality"),
                          levels = c("High quality", "Medium quality")),
         id = factor(id, levels = bin_quality$id[order(!str_starts(bin_quality$id, "R"), bin_quality$id)])) %>%
  plot_ly(x = ~id, y = ~MAGs, color = ~Quality, colors = c(site_teal, "#6b7588"), type = "bar",
          hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y} MAGs<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>") %>%
  layout(barmode = "stack", xaxis = list(title = "", tickangle = -90, tickfont = list(size = 10)),
         yaxis = list(title = "MAGs recovered"), legend = list(traceorder = "normal")) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

## Phylogenomic placement and enzyme repertoires

The MAGs were placed on a tree built from a concatenated alignment of 400
PhyloPhlAn marker genes. Closely related database genomes were included for
context. The rings show each genome's count of algal CAZymes, sulfatases and
peptidoglycanases, and whether the MAG came from a fish gut or a bioreactor.

```{r phylo-tree}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-cap: "PhyloPhlAn tree of *Kyphosus* MAGs and database relatives. Clades are shaded by phylum, the bar ring shows enzyme counts, and the outer ring shows where each MAG came from."
hl <- tribble(
  ~node, ~Taxonomy,
  355, "Alphaproteobacteria", 213, "Bacillota", 281, "Bacteroidota",
  356, "Desulfovibrionales", 204, "Gammaproteobacteria", 153, "Fibrobacterota",
  212, "Fusobacteriota", 210, "Spirochaetota", 152, "WOR-3", 350, "Verrucomicrobiota")

tree <- read.newick(kd("RAxML_bestTree.all_proteins_refined.tre"))
tree <- ape::root(tree, node = 209)

cazy_long <- bin_cazy %>%
  pivot_longer(-bins, names_to = "Enzyme", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(Enzyme = recode(Enzyme, "Red Algae CaZy" = "Red algal CAZymes",
                         "Brown Algae CaZy" = "Brown algal CAZymes",
                         "Green Algae CaZy" = "Green algal CAZymes",
                         "Peptidogylcanases" = "Peptidoglycanases"),
         Enzyme = factor(Enzyme, levels = c("Red algal CAZymes", "Brown algal CAZymes",
                                            "Green algal CAZymes", "Sulfatases", "Peptidoglycanases")))

p <- ggtree(tree, layout = "fan", open.angle = 15, colour = "grey80", linewidth = .25)
p <- rotate_tree(ggtree::rotate(ggtree::rotate(p, 209), 208), 90)
p +
  geom_highlight(data = hl, aes(node = node, fill = Taxonomy), extendto = .715,
                 alpha = .9, to.bottom = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tax_colors, name = "MAG taxonomy",
                    guide = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 2)) +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_fruit(data = cazy_long, geom = geom_bar, stat = "identity", orientation = "y",
             mapping = aes(x = count, y = bins, fill = Enzyme), pwidth = .35,
             axis.params = list(axis = "x", text.size = 1.8, nbreak = 3, text.colour = site_text)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("indianred1", "#b38f3a", "darkgreen", "gold", "orange"),
                    name = "Enzyme class", guide = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 2)) +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_fruit(data = bin_source, geom = geom_col, mapping = aes(y = bins, x = dummy, fill = Source),
             pwidth = .05) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Fish Gut" = "#4472C4", "Bioreactor" = "#A6A6A6",
                               "Database Relative" = "#3d4452"),
                    name = "MAG source", guide = guide_legend(order = 3)) +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.key = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.text = element_text(colour = site_text, size = 11),
        legend.title = element_text(colour = site_text, size = 12, face = "bold"),
        legend.key.size = unit(.45, "cm"),
        legend.position = "right", legend.box = "vertical",
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

### Enzyme counts per MAG

Each point is a genome. Use the menu to change the enzyme class on the y-axis. Bacteroidota are the most versatile and
include the largest sulfatase sets, up to 297 in one genome. A few Bacillota
(*Vallitalea*) and Verrucomicrobiota (Kiritimatiellales) MAGs also have
unusually large and distinctive repertoires.

```{r mag-scatter}
#| fig-height: 5.5
enzyme_cols <- c("Red Algae CaZy", "Brown Algae CaZy", "Green Algae CaZy", "Sulfatases")
pd <- study_mags %>% mutate(`Genome size (Mb)` = `Genome size (bp)` / 1e6)
fig <- plot_ly()
for (i in seq_along(enzyme_cols)) {
  col <- enzyme_cols[i]
  fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
    data = pd, x = ~`Genome size (Mb)`, y = pd[[col]], color = ~Taxonomy, colors = tax_colors,
    type = "scatter", mode = "markers", visible = i == 1,
    marker = list(size = 9, opacity = .85, line = list(width = .5, color = "#111")),
    text = ~paste0("<b>", MAG, "</b><br>", Taxonomy, ", ", Source,
                   "<br>", nice(col), ": ", pd[[col]], "<br>CGCs: ", CGCs),
    hoverinfo = "text", legendgroup = ~Taxonomy, showlegend = TRUE)
}
ntax <- n_distinct(pd$Taxonomy)
buttons <- lapply(seq_along(enzyme_cols), function(i) {
  vis <- rep(seq_along(enzyme_cols) == i, each = ntax)
  list(method = "update", label = nice(enzyme_cols[i]),
       args = list(list(visible = vis), list(yaxis = list(title = paste(nice(enzyme_cols[i]), "per MAG"),
                                                            gridcolor = site_grid))))
})
fig %>%
  layout(updatemenus = list(list(buttons = buttons, x = 0, y = 1.15, xanchor = "left",
                                 bgcolor = "#dfe5ec", bordercolor = "#8a93a3", font = list(color = "#111"))),
         xaxis = list(title = "Genome size (Mb)"), yaxis = list(title = "Red algal CAZymes per MAG"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>Phylum</b>"))) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

```{r mag-table}
study_mags %>%
  transmute(MAG, Taxonomy, Source, `Size (Mb)` = `Genome size (bp)` / 1e6, CGCs,
            `Red algal CAZymes` = `Red Algae CaZy`, `Brown algal CAZymes` = `Brown Algae CaZy`,
            `Green algal CAZymes` = `Green Algae CaZy`, Sulfatases, Acetate, Propanoate, Butyrate,
            `Sulfate reduction` = `Sulfate Reduction`, BGCs) %>%
  mutate(across(c(Acetate, Propanoate, Butyrate, `Sulfate reduction`),
                ~ if_else(str_starts(.x, "No marker"), "none", .x))) %>%
  nb_table(page = 8) %>%
  formatRound("Size (Mb)", digits = 2)
```

## Short-chain fatty acid production

The fish get much of their energy from short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) made by
fermentation. gutSMASH was used to find the pathways for each SCFA. Bubble size
is the percentage of MAGs in a lineage that carry the pathway.

```{r scfa}
#| fig-height: 5.5
scfa <- read.delim(kd("scfa_breakdown.tab"), check.names = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(-Taxa, names_to = "Pathway", values_to = "Fraction") %>%
  mutate(Pathway = str_trim(Pathway),
         Product = case_when(str_detect(Pathway, "Butyr|Lysine") ~ "Butyrate",
                             str_detect(Pathway, "Propion") ~ "Propanoate",
                             TRUE ~ "Acetate"),
         Pathway = str_replace_all(Pathway, "Propionate", "Propanoate"),
         # sentence case for product names inside a pathway name ("Pyruvate to Acetate" -> "Pyruvate to acetate")
         Pathway = str_replace_all(Pathway, "(?<=.)\\b(Acetate|Propanoate|Butyrate|Formate)", tolower),
         Pathway = factor(Pathway, levels = unique(Pathway)),
         Taxa = factor(Taxa, levels = rev(c("Bacillota", "Bacteroidota", "Gammaproteobacteria",
                                            "Desulfovibrionales", "Verrucomicrobiota"))))
scfa %>%
  filter(Fraction > 0) %>%
  mutate(Product = factor(Product, levels = c("Acetate", "Propanoate", "Butyrate")),
         Pathway = droplevels(Pathway),
         Pathway = factor(Pathway, levels = rev(levels(Pathway))),
         Taxa = factor(Taxa, levels = rev(levels(Taxa)))) %>%
  plot_ly(x = ~Taxa, y = ~Pathway, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", color = ~Product,
          colors = c(Acetate = "#ee5f5b", Propanoate = "#62c462", Butyrate = "#52adc8"),
          customdata = ~Fraction,
          marker = list(size = ~ 6 + 40 * sqrt(Fraction), sizemode = "diameter", opacity = .85,
                        line = list(color = "#111", width = .5)),
          hovertemplate = "%{x}<br>%{y}<br>%{customdata:.0%} of MAGs<extra></extra>") %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "", side = "top", tickangle = -30), yaxis = list(title = ""),
         margin = list(t = 110),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>Product</b>"), itemsizing = "constant")) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

## Similarity to reference enzymes

Each binned CAZyme and sulfatase was compared against three references: other
MAGs in this study, GenBank nr, and the curated CAZy or SulfAtlas databases.
Across all annotated genes, the median best-hit identity is 63% to GenBank nr,
56% to CAZy and 36% to SulfAtlas. Most are distant from characterized
enzymes, so the *Kyphosus* gut is a likely source of new seaweed-degrading
enzymes.

The plot shows the five CAZyme and five sulfatase families (from the
algal-polysaccharide families analyzed in the paper) whose genes are least
similar to anything in GenBank nr. Their median best-hit identity is about
40 to 60%.

```{r novelty}
#| fig-height: 4.5
nov <- read.delim(kd("cazy_sulf_nr.tsv")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(nr_id, self_id, sulf_id, dbCAN_id), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.x))))
sulf_fams <- c("S1_13","S1_72","S1_19","S1_8","S1_24","S1_4","S1_11","S1_20",
               "S1_15","S1_16","S1_17","S1_28","S1_25","S1_14","S1_27")
cazy_fams <- c("GH16_16","GH86","GH16_11","GH10","GH82","GH50","GH117","GH150",
               "GH16_12","PL40","PL6","PL38","GH29","PL8","GH95")
db_cols <- c("Other MAGs in this study" = "#8cd2d5", "GenBank nr" = "#8a93a3", "CAZy / SulfAtlas" = "#f0c75e")

# the 5 families per class with the lowest median identity to GenBank nr
least_similar <- function(fams) {
  nov %>% filter(annot %in% fams) %>% group_by(annot) %>%
    summarise(med = median(nr_id, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% slice_min(med, n = 5) %>% pull(annot)
}
cz <- least_similar(cazy_fams); sf <- least_similar(sulf_fams)

nov_long <- bind_rows(
  nov %>% filter(annot %in% cz) %>%
    transmute(annot, `Other MAGs in this study` = self_id, `GenBank nr` = nr_id, `CAZy / SulfAtlas` = dbCAN_id),
  nov %>% filter(annot %in% sf) %>%
    transmute(annot, `Other MAGs in this study` = self_id, `GenBank nr` = nr_id, `CAZy / SulfAtlas` = sulf_id)
) %>% pivot_longer(-annot, names_to = "Database", values_to = "Identity") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Identity)) %>%
  mutate(annot = factor(annot, levels = c(cz, sf)),
         Database = factor(Database, levels = names(db_cols)))

plot_ly(nov_long, x = ~annot, y = ~Identity, color = ~Database, colors = db_cols, type = "box",
        boxpoints = FALSE,
        hovertemplate = "%{x}<br>%{y:.1f}% identity<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>") %>%
  layout(boxmode = "group",
         xaxis = list(title = "Enzyme family (least similar first)",
                      categoryorder = "array", categoryarray = c(cz, sf)),
         yaxis = list(title = "% identity to best hit", range = c(20, 102), ticksuffix = "%"),
         shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = 4.5, x1 = 4.5, y0 = 0, y1 = 1, yref = "paper",
                            line = list(dash = "dot", color = "#6b7588"))),
         annotations = list(
           list(x = 2, y = 1.07, yref = "paper", text = "<b>CAZymes</b>", showarrow = FALSE),
           list(x = 7, y = 1.07, yref = "paper", text = "<b>Sulfatases</b>", showarrow = FALSE)),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -.22)) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

## A GH86 β-agarase/β-porphyranase with an undescribed domain

GH86 enzymes cut agar and porphyran, the main glycans of red algae. The gene
tree of binned GH86 sequences has a clade from three different phyla
(Bacillota, Bacteroidota and Verrucomicrobiota) that share an N-terminal region
with no characterized function. Most of these sequences also have a signal
peptide, so they are likely exported. This is consistent with several taxa
breaking these glycans down outside the cell.

```{r gh86}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-cap: "GH86 gene tree. Each tip is one binned GH86 sequence, colored by the phylum of its MAG; filled points have a signal peptide."
gh <- ape::root(ape::read.tree(kd("GH86.tre")), node = 112)
tips <- gh$tip.label
prot <- read.delim(kd("all_cazy_prot_HGT.tab")) %>% filter(prot %in% tips) %>%
  distinct(prot, .keep_all = TRUE)

ggtree(gh, layout = "circular", colour = "grey75", linewidth = .3) %<+% prot +
  geom_tippoint(aes(colour = taxonomy, shape = signalp), size = 3.2, stroke = .9) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Bacillota = "#ff5c5c", Bacteroidota = "#4ea3ff",
                                 Verrucomicrobiota = "#d5b2f7"), na.value = "grey60",
                      name = "Gene taxonomy", guide = guide_legend(order = 1)) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(Y = 16, N = 1), labels = c(Y = "Exported", N = "Not exported"),
                     na.value = 4, name = "Signal peptide") +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.key = element_rect(fill = site_bg, colour = NA),
        legend.text = element_text(colour = site_text, size = 12),
        legend.title = element_text(colour = site_text, size = 13, face = "bold"),
        plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
```

::: {.paper-figure}
![The published GH86 figure, which aligns each sequence against the tree. Green: signal peptide; magenta: the undescribed N-terminal region; grey: catalytic domain.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AaronAOliver/KyphosusMAGs/main/figures/GH86_gene_alignment.svg){fig-align="center" width="85%"}
:::

## Biosynthetic gene clusters

antiSMASH found `r nrow(bin_bgc)` biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) in the MAGs.
BiG-SLiCE then measured each one's distance to the nearest known gene cluster
family (GCF). Clusters above the dotted line at a distance of 900 are counted as
novel.

The sunburst groups the clusters by antiSMASH class (inner ring) and product
type (outer ring). Click a class to zoom in.

```{r bgc-sunburst}
#| fig-height: 5
cls_map <- c(RiPPs = "RiPP", NRPS = "NRPS", Terpene = "Terpene", PKSI = "PKS", PKSother = "PKS",
             Saccharides = "Other", `PKS-NRP_Hybrids` = "Other", Others = "Other")
bgc <- bin_bgc %>% mutate(Class = recode(class, !!!cls_map),
                          product = str_replace_all(product, ";", " / "))
sb <- bind_rows(
  bgc %>% count(Class) %>% transmute(ids = Class, labels = Class, parents = "", n),
  bgc %>% count(Class, product) %>% transmute(ids = paste(Class, product, sep = "-"),
                                              labels = product, parents = Class, n)
)
plot_ly(sb, ids = ~ids, labels = ~labels, parents = ~parents, values = ~n,
        type = "sunburst", branchvalues = "total",
        hovertemplate = "<b>%{label}</b><br>%{value} BGCs<extra></extra>",
        marker = list(colors = NULL)) %>%
  dark_layout(margin = list(t = 10, b = 10, l = 10, r = 10),
              sunburstcolorway = c("#8cd2d5", "#ee5f5b", "#f89406", "#62c462", "#b38bd6"),
              extendsunburstcolors = TRUE)
```

```{r bgc-distance}
#| fig-height: 4.5
set.seed(1)
bgc %>%
  mutate(x = as.numeric(factor(Class, levels = c("RiPP", "NRPS", "Terpene", "PKS", "Other"))),
         xj = x + runif(n(), -.3, .3)) %>%
  plot_ly(x = ~xj, y = ~distance, color = ~completeness,
          colors = c(Complete = site_teal, Fragmented = "#6b7588"),
          type = "scatter", mode = "markers", marker = list(size = 7, opacity = .8),
          text = ~paste0("<b>", product, "</b><br>", MAG, "<br>", taxonomy,
                         "<br>distance to nearest GCF: ", distance),
          hoverinfo = "text") %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "", tickvals = 1:5, ticktext = c("RiPP", "NRPS", "Terpene", "PKS", "Other")),
         yaxis = list(title = "BiG-SLiCE distance to nearest GCF"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>BGC</b>")),
         shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = .5, x1 = 5.5, y0 = 900, y1 = 900,
                            line = list(dash = "dot", color = "#ee5f5b"))),
         annotations = list(list(x = 0.5, y = 900, xanchor = "left", yanchor = "bottom", showarrow = FALSE,
                                 text = "novelty threshold (900)", bgcolor = "rgba(37,42,52,.85)",
                                 font = list(color = "#ee5f5b", size = 11)))) %>%
  dark_layout()
```

## Takeaways

- Bacteroidota MAGs carry the widest range of algal-polysaccharide enzymes,
  but few single genomes can fully break down any one sulfated algal glycan.
- The enzymes needed are split across lineages, and many have signal peptides,
  suggesting that *Kyphosus* symbionts degrade seaweed jointly, outside the
  cell.
- Many of the CAZymes, sulfatases and BGCs are distant from characterized
  references, so these bioreactor communities are a source of new enzymes.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
